learn: The vowels are a, e, i, o and u. Every word has at least one vowel.
Short a says /a/ as in cat. Short e says /e/ as in bed. Short i says /i/ as in pig.
Short o says /o/ as in hot. Short u says /u/ as in sun.
lessons.try: Say each short vowel sound and think of one word for each.

learn: A blend is two consonants side by side. You can hear both sounds.
In "stop", you hear /s/ and /t/. In "frog", you hear /f/ and /r/.
Other start blends are bl, cl, gr, tr, sl and sp.
check: Which word starts with a blend?
lessons.try: Read these words: flag, crab, spin, slug, drum.

learn: Blends can come at the end of a word too.
"Hand" ends with nd. "Lamp" ends with mp. "Best" ends with st.
Say the word slowly so you can hear every sound.
check: How do you hear every sound in a word?
lessons.try: Read and write: tent, milk, jump, desk, list.

learn: A digraph is two letters that make one new sound.
s and h together say /sh/ as in ship and fish.
c and h together say /ch/ as in chin and lunch.
check: Two letters that make one sound
lessons.try: Find three things at home that have sh or ch in their names.

learn: t and h together say /th/ as in thumb and bath.
w and h together say /w/ as in when and whale.
Many question words start with wh: what, when, where, why and which.
check: Which is a wh question word?
What sound does th make in "thumb"?
lessons.try: Ask a family member three questions that start with wh.

learn: c and k together say /k/ at the end of short words like duck, sock and back.
n and g together say /ng/ as in sing, ring and king.
Digraphs help you read many more words.
check: What sound does ck make in "duck"?
lessons.try: Read: duck, rock, sing, long, sick, wing.

lessons.t: Magic E Makes a Vowel Long
learn: When a word ends in e after one consonant, the e is silent.
The silent e makes the vowel before it say its name. This is a long vowel.
"Cap" becomes "cape". "Kit" becomes "kite".
check: Makes the vowel say its name
Can you hear the e at the end of "kite"?
lessons.try: Write "tap", then add an e. Read the new word.

learn: a with silent e: cake, game, lake.
i with silent e: bike, time, five.
o with silent e: home, rope, nose.
lessons.try: Read: rake, ride, bone, gate, pine, hole.

learn: u with silent e can say /yoo/ as in cube and mule, or /oo/ as in tube and flute.
e with silent e is less common: Pete, these.
When you see a word ending in e, try the long vowel first.
check: When a word ends in silent e, try...
lessons.try: Read: cute, rule, these, June.

learn: Sometimes two vowels work together. We call them a vowel team.
ai says long a in the middle of words: rain, tail, paint.
ay says long a at the end: day, play, say.
check: What sound does ai make in "rain"?
At the end of a word
Which word has a vowel team?
lessons.try: Read: mail, train, stay, gray, wait.

learn: ee says long e: see, tree, feet.
ea often says long e too: eat, read, sea.
A rule to remember: when two vowels go walking, the first one often does the talking.
check: Which word has ea saying long e?
"When two vowels go walking," the first one...
lessons.try: Read: sheep, beach, green, leaf, meet.

learn: oa says long o: boat, coat, road.
ow can say long o: snow, grow, slow.
igh says long i: night, light, high.
lessons.try: Read: goat, show, bright, toad, flight.

learn: Some words appear so often that we learn them by sight.
Words like the, said, was, have, they and could do not always follow the rules.
Knowing them quickly helps you read smoothly.
check: Do sight words always follow the rules?
lessons.try: Practise reading these until they are fast: the, said, was, they, have, what.

learn: Good readers make their voice match the story.
A question mark means your voice goes up. An exclamation mark means read with feeling.
A period means stop for a short breath.
check: What does a question mark tell your voice?
What does an exclamation mark mean?
lessons.try: Read "Oh no!" and "Is it you?" with the right voice.

learn: If a sentence does not make sense, go back and read it again.
Ask: Does that look right? Does that sound right? Does that make sense?
Rereading helps you fix mistakes and understand more.
check: What do you do if a sentence does not make sense?
lessons.try: Read a page of a book twice. Notice how the second time is smoother.

learn: A noun is a word for a person, place or thing.
Teacher, park and ball are nouns.
Names of special people and places, like Maya or Texas, start with a capital letter.
check: Which noun needs a capital letter?
lessons.try: Find five nouns in your room.

learn: Add s to most nouns to show more than one: cat, cats.
Add es to words that end in s, x, ch or sh: box, boxes; dish, dishes.
Some words change: one child, two children.
lessons.try: Write the "more than one" word for: dog, fox, bus, cup.

learn: A verb is an action word. It tells what someone does.
Jump, eat, read and swim are verbs.
Add ed to show it already happened: jump, jumped.
lessons.try: Act out three verbs and have someone guess them.

learn: A sentence is a complete thought.
It tells who or what, and what they do: The dog runs.
It starts with a capital letter and ends with a mark.
lessons.try: Write a sentence about your favourite food.

learn: A telling sentence ends with a period.
An asking sentence ends with a question mark.
A sentence with strong feeling ends with an exclamation mark.
lessons.try: Write one telling, one asking and one excited sentence.

learn: Adjectives describe nouns: the big, brown dog.
Details make writing more interesting to read.
We can join two ideas with and, but or because: I was tired, so I went to bed.
check: The fluffy cat slept in the sun.
lessons.try: Make "The cat sat." more interesting by adding two describing words.

learn: Characters are the people or animals in a story.
The setting is where and when the story happens.
Authors give clues about characters through what they say and do.
check: The people or animals in a story
Where and when the story happens
How do we learn about characters?
lessons.try: Name the characters and setting of a story you read this week.

learn: Stories have a beginning, a middle and an end.
Often there is a problem in the middle that the characters must solve.
In "The Little Red Hen", the hen asks for help, nobody helps, so she does the work herself and eats the bread.
check: Where is the problem often found?
In "The Little Red Hen", who makes the bread?
Which words help retell a story?
lessons.try: Retell a story you know using first, next, then and last.

learn: Many stories teach a lesson, called a moral.
Aesop's fable "The Tortoise and the Hare" teaches that slow and steady wins the race.
Think about what a character learned by the end.
check: Who wins in "The Tortoise and the Hare"?
The lesson of that fable is...
Slow and steady wins the race
lessons.try: Tell someone the lesson of a story you like.

learn: Fiction stories are made up. Nonfiction tells true facts.
A book about real sharks is nonfiction. A story about a talking shark is fiction.
We read nonfiction to learn.
check: A story about a talking shark is...
lessons.try: Find one fiction and one nonfiction book.

learn: Nonfiction books have helpers called text features.
A title tells the topic. Headings tell what each part is about. Captions explain pictures.
A table of contents tells which page each part is on.
check: What tells which page a part is on?
lessons.try: Find a heading and a caption in a nonfiction book.

learn: The main topic is what the whole text is about.
Key details are facts that tell more about the main topic.
In a text about frogs, a key detail might be "Frogs start life as tadpoles."
check: What the whole text is about
Which is a key detail about frogs?
lessons.try: Read a short nonfiction page. Say the main topic and two details.

learn: An opinion is what you think or feel.
When you write an opinion, say what you think and give a reason.
"I think cats are the best pets because they are soft and quiet."
check: What should go with an opinion?
lessons.try: Write your opinion about your favourite season and one reason.

learn: Informative writing teaches facts about a topic.
Name the topic, give some facts, then write an ending.
"Bees are insects. They make honey. They help flowers grow. Bees are helpful."
check: Which is a fact about bees?
lessons.try: Write three facts about an animal you know.

learn: A narrative tells about something that happened, in order.
Use words like first, then and at the end.
Tell how you felt. Then share your writing with a friend and listen to their ideas.
lessons.try: Write about something fun you did, in three parts.
